reading.title: The Ferry to Gull Island
reading.purpose: Cross a stormy sea with Kai and discover why a garden on a rocky island is hard to grow.
paras: Kai had never visited his uncle Rafael's lighthouse, and the ferry ride felt long. The water was turbulent, and waves slapped the side of the boat. When a tempest, a violent storm with strong wind, rolled in from the west, the captain steered for the nearest dock.
By the time they landed, the rain had stopped. Gull Island was rugged, a place of rocky slopes and steep paths. Jagged stones stuck out of the grass, with sharp, uneven points like broken teeth.

Uncle Rafael led the way up the hill. "Walk where I walk," he said. "The path is treacherous after rain, because the mud hides loose stones." Kai stepped carefully. The climb looked formidable at first, but it took only twenty minutes.

At the top, the ground was barren, with only sand, rock, and a few patches of dry moss. Rafael explained that the wind was harsh and made young plants wither, drying up and shriveling before they could flower.

Kai pulled a bag of seeds from his pocket. "Then we build a wall of stones to block the wind," he said. Rafael laughed. "That trip sounded perilous, full of danger, and you still want to plant seeds? You are a true islander."

qs.q: In paragraph 3, the word "treacherous" describes a path that is
choices: dangerous because it is very steep and long
easy to follow because it is well marked
crowded with visitors and island workers
qs.why: Rafael says the path is treacherous "because the mud hides loose stones," so the danger is hidden.

qs.q: Which sentence shows why few plants grow on the hilltop?
choices: Kai pulled a bag of seeds from his pocket.
Uncle Rafael led the way up the hill.
By the time they landed, the rain had stopped.
Rafael explained that the wind was harsh and made young plants wither, drying up and shriveling before they could flower.
qs.why: Only this sentence gives the reason: the harsh wind makes young plants dry up before they can flower.

ev.text: Rafael explained that the wind was harsh and made young plants wither, drying up and shriveling before they could flower.

qs.q: Why did Uncle Rafael tell Kai to walk where he walked?
choices: He knew which spots on the path were safe.
He wanted to show Kai a shortcut through the grass.
He was worried that Kai would drop the bag of seeds.
He planned to take photographs of Kai's footprints.
qs.why: Rafael knows the island, and the mud hides loose stones, so following his steps keeps Kai safe.

qs.q: What is the best summary of this story?
choices: A boy is sent home from an island because of a violent storm.
A boy climbs a lighthouse to rescue a ferry from the rocks.
A boy visits a rugged island in a storm and plans a garden.
A boy and his uncle build a ferry dock on the barren hilltop.
qs.why: Kai crosses rough water, climbs the rocky island, and ends by planning a garden with a wind wall.

clues.text: a violent storm with strong wind
sharp, uneven points like broken teeth
only sand, rock, and a few patches of dry moss
